units.translation: ⟦1⟧. = ⟦2⟧. ⟦3⟧., as at ⟦4⟧ ⟦5⟧, and often. The ⟦6⟧ on Delos, where Apollo was born, is mentioned ⟦7⟧. ⟦8⟧ and elsewhere; in ⟦9⟧ (the cliffs and rocks, naturally not Mount Cynthus) lies, as a scholiast correctly observes, also the reason why Apollo exchanged Delos for Delphi. (⟦10⟧ ⟦11⟧, Weckl.). On line 10 the scholiast emphasizes that Aeschylus, as an Athenian, makes Apollo take this route, whereas the Boeotian Pindar has him go via Tanagra (in whose territory Delium lay; hardly correct, O. Müller Orchom. p. 147 ⟦12⟧). But sea traffic (cf. ⟦13⟧) went from the Cyclades far more to Attica than to the Boeotian coast. Also in the paean of Aristonous, where the purification in Tempe is mentioned, it says (19f.): ⟦14⟧ (19f.); deliberately therefore here ⟦15⟧, and cf. 21. — 11.
when Pallas sent him to Pytho
the capture of Ilium and its destruction
seats and hiding places of the just land

In passing, a service of Athens to civilization is highlighted: the Athenians, who first learned the arts from Hephaestus and Athena (⟦1⟧ B), also first made a road through the wilderness. This is the sacred road for the sacred embassies to Delphi (⟦2⟧), on which (Schol.) people still went ahead with axes, ⟦3⟧.
as if they would tame the land
⟦1⟧ are the Athenians as sons of Erichthonius, at the same time also with reference to the forged axes.

On ⟦1⟧ the scholiast on line 2 supplies the mythological background: a son of Poseidon and Melaina, who was a granddaughter of Deucalion. — ⟦2⟧ also at 765, hardly a normal word, but coined after the model of ⟦3⟧ to match ⟦4⟧. ⟦5⟧ of the ruler, ⟦6⟧.
holding the helm at the stern of the city

⟦1⟧ of the art of prophecy ⟦2⟧; here constructed differently (⟦3⟧ as at ⟦4⟧) and with some harshness, in that the god ⟦5⟧. On ⟦6⟧ with double accusative see on ⟦7⟧; here there is additionally a double object, ⟦8⟧ — ⟦9⟧, as at 88 ⟦10⟧ (Minckwitz). ⟦11⟧ (manuscript) can be understood of the present holder; however ⟦12⟧ (Kirchhoff) is highly recommended, especially by line 3 ⟦13⟧. In line 19 a main thought is expressed, which recurs at 616ff., 713; see also Frg. 82 (⟦14⟧): ⟦15⟧, and cf. (Weckl.) ⟦16⟧ ⟦17⟧, ⟦18⟧, ⟦19⟧. Thus as the Pythia stands to Apollo, so he stands to Zeus: a proclaimer, nothing more.
